articles.title: Tinto Brass obituary
articles.summary: Italian director drawn to the erotic best known for his 1979 film Caligula, which is now regarded as a cult favourite. No matter how one defines the films of the director Tinto Brass, who has died aged 93, they manage, in most cases, to keep a distance, however narrowly, from pornography.
body: There is no doubt that most of his two dozen features, the most notorious being Salon Kitty (1976) and Caligula (1979), could be variously labelled sexploitation (the female nude shown purely for sexual or commercial reasons), sexist, softcore (no erections or ejaculations), kitsch (bad taste) and camp (“its essence being its love of the unnatural: of artifice and exaggeration”, in Susan Sontag ’s definition).

If a director who has a personal stamp, and whose oeuvre has a thematic and stylistic consistency, is considered an auteur, then Brass, who wrote and edited his own films, would qualify. Needless to say, he was in a different category from Federico Fellini, whom he idolised; Luchino Visconti, whom he parodied; and Roberto Rossellini, for whom he was assistant on two films. Yet, in the early 1960s, Brass was thought of as one of the most interesting directors of the new generation.

articles.title: ‘The Peanut Butter Falcon’ Breakout Zack Gottsagen and Anna Enger Ritch to Star in ‘A Reason to Stay’ From Director Rippin Sindher (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: The film recently wrapped principal photography in Ohio. The project reunites Gottsagen with TVACOM Films’ Davied Thiews after their collaboration on “The Peanut Butter
body: “The Peanut Butter Falcon” breakout Zack Gottsagen and “S.W.A.T.” star Anna Enger Ritch will star as brother and sister in “A Reason to Stay,” a new romantic comedy from Rippin Sindher. The film recently wrapped principal photography in Ohio.

Per an official logline, “A Reason to Stay,” which Sindher co-wrote with Melanie Forchetti, follows “Zach (Gottsagen), a young man with Down syndrome who helps run his family’s struggling animal shelter alongside his sister Sophie (Ritch), who returns home following their mother’s death. As Sophie confronts the life she left behind, an unexpected reunion with a former love forces her to decide whether to return to the future she planned or embrace a second chance at home.” Spencer Neville also stars.

After breaking out with her 2025 short, “Flight 182,” Sindher makes her feature directorial debut with “A Reason to Stay.” In April, she was named as one of seven fellows for the Sundance Institute’s Cultural Impact Residency.

articles.title: Adobe Premiere Mobile App Launches With Hundreds of Thousands of Tracks Licensed From UMG, WMG
articles.summary: Adobe has just made it easier for creators to add some of their favorite hot jams to short-form video clips. On Tuesday, the free Adobe Premiere mobile app, designed for creators to make videos for platforms like YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels, added hundreds of thousands of songs…
body: Top-trending tracks avaliable in the app at launch include: Olivia Dean’s “So Easy (To Fall In Love)”; Sombr’s “Homewrecker”; Chappell Roan’s “Good Luck, Babe!”; Justin Bieber’s “Daisies”; Lady Gaga’s “The Dead Dance”; Ava Max’s “Sweet but Psycho”; Vance Joy’s “Riptide”; OneRepublic’s “Counting Stars”; and Teddy Swims’ “Lose Control.”

Users of Premiere on mobile can browse, search and preview trending music by artist or track; filter by genre and duration; bookmark favorites; and explore popular music through label-featured collections. Once they select a track, they can then add up to 60 seconds directly to their video. In addition, Premiere mobile provides customizable templates paired with music.
“Adobe hasn’t built the music muscle before this,” Jay LeBoeuf, Adobe head of AI audio for creators, told Variety in an interview at the Adobe MAX creativity conference in Miami.

articles.summary: HBO’s “Harry Potter” showrunner Francesca Gardiner is condemning the “abuse” being directed at Paapa Essiedu, the “I May Destroy You” Emmy nominee who is taking over the role of Professor Severus Snape in the first television series adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s literary franchise.
body: HBO ‘s “ Harry Potter ” showrunner Francesca Gardiner is condemning the “abuse” being directed at Paapa Essiedu, the “I May Destroy You” Emmy nominee who is taking over the role of Professor Severus Snape in the first television series adaptation of J.K. Rowling ‘s literary franchise. Essiedu has been outspoken since March about the racism he’s been facing online by toxic fans upset with the casting of a Black actor in the role.

Essiedu told the publication that he is more than open to criticism when it is warranted, explaining: “There’s some people who are just like, ‘I’ve done my research, and I know what kind of actor you are, and you suck.’ And they’re totally entitled to their opinion. But then there are the people who are like, ‘You are bad because you are Black’—which, to me, is racist.. Well, actually not ‘You’re bad because you are Black.’ But there is a racially driven animosity.”
Essiedu first spoke to The Sunday Times in March about the racially motivated death threats he was getting online over his casting as Snape.

articles.title: David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct after losing injunction bid
articles.summary: ITN and the Guardian allege the comedian preyed on teenage girls and young women. He has denied all allegations.
body: ITV News and the Guardian have published reports alleging that David Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women, including one who was aged 15.

The allegations were made as a part of a joint three-year investigation, external by the two news organisations, which was published after the entertainer lost a legal bid to stop the claims against him being made public.
Some of the women accuse Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers. One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15-years- old as a "sexual assault".
In a letter to journalists published by the Guardian, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

articles.title: ‘I’m looking for faces which surprise me’: how Richard Avedon photographed the soul of his subjects
articles.summary: Ron Howard’s illuminating Netflix documentary looks back on the career of one of America’s most inventive and versatile photographers. Richard Avedon had only taken a couple of frames when he accidentally hit his head on a light being held above him. The Dalai Lama burst into laughter.
body: Avedon’s assistant, Sebastian Kim, was baffled. “I was like, what the hell happened? There’s only four frames out of a roll of 12 frames,” he recalls in a phone interview. “I realised he knew at that moment that something had happened, a mistake had happened: he hit his head and the Dalai Lama lit up.”

Kim, 52, now an eminent photographer in his own right, is among the interviewees who feature in a new documentary, Avedon, directed by Oscar winner Ron Howard, which premiered at the Cannes film festival and is released on Netflix this week.

The film explores the six-decade career of the fashion and portrait photographer renowned for white backgrounds that stripped away distractions and for capturing figures ranging from Marilyn Monroe and Charlie Chaplin to civil rights activists, anti-war protesters and working-class Americans.

Avedon was raised in New York City. His father, Jacob Avedon, co-founded a specialty store on Fifth Avenue, which was lost overnight during the Great Depression. Avedon struggled academically, flunking out of high school despite winning a citywide poetry prize.

articles.title: Cerys Matthews pays tribute to her family as she receives OBE
articles.summary: Matthews was behind the Welsh rock band Catatonia who shot to fame during the "Cool Cymru" movement of the 1990s.
body: Singer and presenter Cerys Matthews paid tribute to her family as she received an OBE.
Matthews, from Cardiff, was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) for services to music and received a medal from the Prince of Wales.
Speaking after the ceremony, Matthews said she accepted the OBE in memory of her family and "in gratitude of the freedoms I have as a female in this era".
Matthews' voice is also familiar to many over her Christmas holidays because of her 1999 rendition of Baby It's Cold Outside, sung with Sir Tom Jones.

articles.title: Even Martin Scorsese uses AI for storyboards. Can the art survive?
articles.summary: As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost.
body: Usually, storyboards are made together by a director, an artist and other crew members responsible for the film’s visual storytelling, such as cinematographers, editors, production designers, stunt co-ordinators and more. “I find it very fulfilling to make art in such a collaborative way,” says Alex Clark, a British storyboard artist whose recent films include Bong Joon Ho’s sci-fi comedy Mickey 17, adventure romance The Gorge and Louis Leterrier’s recent thriller The Last House. “It’s about people sitting down to discuss each other’s ideas. You might act things out, make sound effects, read dialogue. You develop a creative relationship with one another.”

articles.title: ‘Confession’ Review: Rob Lowe and James Franco in a Ben Shapiro-Scripted, Stalinist Russia-Set Drama That’s Terminally Tedious
articles.summary: Jennifer Jason Leigh, Nick Nolte, Emile Hirsch and Kodi Smit-McPhee also appear in Václav Marhoul's film about the brutal interrogation of a prisoner in a Stalin-era Russian jail.
body: Reviewing the new movie scripted by Ben Shapiro, I’m tempted to pan it on ideological grounds. The screenwriter, after all, is the controversial right-wing political commentator who co-founded The Daily Wire and was editor-at-large at Breitbart News for several years. To say that the vast majority of his views are loathsome to me is an understatement.

Other than its hardly controversial stance that Stalinist Russia was a very, very bad place, there’s nothing inherently political about the film. Except possibly for the casting of James Franco in a major role, which, like the presence of Jonathan Majors in the company’s recent Run Hide Fight: Infidels, seems designed to give a middle finger to the Hollywood studios for shunning them. In this case, Franco has plenty of distinguished company, with the ensemble including Rob Lowe, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Nick Nolte, Emile Hirsch, Brad Dourif, Dean Norris, and Kodi Smit-McPhee. The story behind that casting would likely prove more interesting than the film itself.
points: Jennifer Jason Leigh, Nick Nolte, Emile Hirsch and Kodi Smit-McPhee also appear in Václav Marhoul's film about the brutal interrogation of a prisoner in a Stalin-era Russian jail.
